title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). S is a base with 2 invertible and E_0/S an elliptic curve. Σ_J = E_0/{±1} is the Kummer line (a P^1-bundle). D_J ⊂ Σ_J is the image of the three nonzero 2-torsion sections (J), and t(S) is the image of the origin. Grothendieck considers pairs (E,σ), equivalently (E_0, I), where E → E_0 ≅ E/M_0 is étale principal with group V = M_0 = 2E_0 ≅ (Z/2)^2_S locally. Here I is a V-torsor of 'points of order 4 over 2-torsion', and X = E/σ.

Diagram (29). E → E_0 is étale. E_0 → Σ_J is branched over D_J ∪ t(S). E → X is branched over the points of I. X → Σ_J is branched over D_J. Δ = X|D_J consists of 6 points, the octahedral configuration: images of the 4-torsion points that are not 2-torsion, grouped in ± pairs.

This page.
(i) Diagram (29) is cartesian over Σ_J* = Σ_J \ D_J, where X* is an étale V-torsor just as E is over E_0.
(ii) It is not cartesian near D_J. E_0/Σ_J is ramified there, whereas E/X is unramified at Δ, since the points of Δ are not fixed by σ. If the square were cartesian there, flat base change along the finite flat X → Σ_J, plus descent, would make E_0/Σ_J étale at D_J. That is a contradiction.
(iii) Hence the whole diagram is reconstructed from E_0 → Σ (with Σ ⊃ D_J and the extension of Σ*) together with a degenerate (branched) V-cover X → Σ. So the datum (E,σ), i.e. (E_0, I), is equivalent to E_0 plus such a cover X. This yields a sheaf K with I ≅ K ∧ (X|t), i.e. I is the twist of K by the fibre of X over t.
(iv) Conclusion: the torsor I is 'poudre aux yeux' (window dressing). One loses nothing by taking E = E_0, σ = σ_0, I = V = 2E_0 = M_0, the trivial torsor. Then X = Σ_J and X → Σ_J becomes a canonical self-map of Σ_J.

The next page identifies this self-map as the map induced by multiplication by 2 on E_0, i.e. the Lattès map. It is to be characterised purely in terms of J and the section t, via the Klein four-group of involutions of P^1 permuting {t} ∪ J, with f(fixed points of σ_i^t) = ξ_i. Riemann–Hurwitz confirms the picture: a (Z/2)^2-Galois cover P^1 → P^1 branched at 3 points with all indices 2 has genus 0, and its 6 ramification points form the octahedron.
errors: No mathematical error found. The non-cartesianness argument at D_J is correct: E→X is unramified at Δ because the 4-torsion points that are not 2-torsion are not fixed by -1, while E_0→Σ_J is ramified over D_J; X→Σ_J is finite flat, so descent applies.
Minor imprecision: the identification 'data (E,σ) ⇔ E_0 + cover X' is stated loosely ('il doit être facile de vérifier'); the precise category equivalence, including the sheaf K, is not written out.

ideas.what: Multiplication by 2 on E_0 descends to a degree-4 self-map of the Kummer line, which is the quotient of P^1 by the Klein four-group of 2-torsion translations, branched over the 3 nonzero 2-torsion images, with ramification at an octahedral 6-point configuration.
ideas.modern_name: Lattès map / Kummer-line doubling; Klein four-group action on P^1

ideas.what: Failure of cartesianness of the square E→E_0 over X→Σ at the branch locus, proved by flat descent.
ideas.modern_name: Base change of ramified covers / descent of étaleness

ideas.what: Reduction of an auxiliary level datum (V-torsor I) to the trivial case: the torsor is recovered as a twist I ≅ K ∧ (X|t), so the moduli problem reduces to E_0 plus a branched V-cover of its Kummer line.
ideas.modern_name: Twisting by torsors; level-2/level-4 structures via Kummer line covers

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a routine verification inside a private reconstruction of level structures on elliptic curves via the Kummer line. The resulting Lattès map, Klein four-group action and octahedral configuration are classical, and the descent argument is standard.
transcription_corrections: 'or si c'était contraire[?]' should almost certainly read 'or si c'était cartésien'; likewise 'qui est contexte[?]' on the previous page reads 'qui est cartésien au dessus de Σ_J*'.
'(car dessus[?] auquel X* est étale principal...' is likely '(car au-dessus duquel X* est étale principal de groupe V, tel comme E sur E_0)'.
'Quand[?] = il doit' is probably 'Conclusion: il doit'.
'd'où un faisceau[?] K' is plausibly correct ('faisceau' or 'fibré'); I ≃ K ∧ (X|t).
'on ne perd[?] rien[?] par le cas[?]' is probably 'on ne perd rien en généralité'.
